newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close lower on political concerns.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close lower on political concerns.

text.p: Shares on the Delhi stock exchange closed sharply lower on nervous selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) after parliament was forced to adjourn for a second successive day, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 9.37 points down at 676.16.

The opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party forced the adjournment of parliament for the second consecutive day on Thursday with a noisy protest over the political stalemate in India's northern state of Uttar Pradesh.
Brokers said a weaker than expected results of some weighted stocks, in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March), also dampened the buying interest.

"Flow of poor working results by some blue-chip companies for the first-half of the current financial year have an opportinity to bear operators to regain charge of the market," said Vijay Agarwal of brokers Mass Financial Services.
ACC lost 42.65 rupees at 1,151 while Reliance Industries ended 3.10 rupees down at 178.60.
TELCO lost 12 rupees at 375 and Hindustan Lever quoted 8.50 rupees lower at 808.
